tools.name: analyze_audio
tools.description: Analyze original source audio from cached waveform peaks; local, read-only, no model. Returns bounded peak/RMS waveform bins, onset candidates and signed energy changes (dB), all in source µs (`src_*`), plus resolution and event counts. Choose music edit/alignment points, including outside a clip's trim. These are amplitude measurements, not beats, bars or melody recognition. At most 60 s per call; max_points affects only the summary. Peaks are cache-limited, not true-peak or LUFS. To land `src_us` at timeline T on a layer: `src_in_us = src_us - (T - t_start_us) * rate` (`rate` from project://tracks, 1 when absent).

max_points.description: Maximum waveform summary bins, 1..1000 (default 200). Does not change event detection resolution.

media_id.description: Imported Audio or Video media id; analyzes its original audio before mix/effects.

onset_threshold_db.description: Minimum short-time energy rise for onset candidates, 1..30 dB (default 6). Candidates are not beats or melody labels.

src_end_us.description: Source-absolute end, exclusive. Default start + 60 seconds, capped at media end. At most 60 seconds per call.

src_start_us.description: Source-absolute start in microseconds, inclusive. Default 0.

tools.name: detect_pauses
tools.description: Find the pauses in the audio a clip plays — the stretches nobody is speaking — from the pre-computed waveform. Read-only: the writes are `remove_pauses` (cut them, or a reviewed subset via its `pauses`) and `create_tacks` (point the user at them). A pause is a run where every channel's peak stays below `threshold_db` (dBFS, default -34) for at least `min_pause_us` (default 500000); a louder run under 80 ms inside it (a click, a cough) does not end it. `layer_id` is an Audio layer, or a VideoClip, read through the linked Audio member that plays (refused when it plays no sound). Returns `{ pauses: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us }], noise_floor_db, peaks_source }`, timeline µs, sorted; `noise_floor_db` is the 10th-percentile peak (null in silence; a threshold reads well 6 dB above it); `peaks_source` is "raw" or "fx" (baked effect chain). Refused (`DerivativeNotReady` with the waveform's `state`) until ready: retry after `retry_after_s`; `failed` names its reason.

layer_id.description:
Target Audio layer id. A VideoClip id is accepted by the host, which
resolves it to the Audio layer of its link before the call.

min_pause_us.description: Shortest pause to surface, in microseconds. Default 500000 (0.5s).

threshold_db.description:
Peak threshold, dBFS (≤ 0). Anything strictly below it counts as
quiet. Default -34.

tools.name: analyze_clip
tools.description: Shots and defect spans of a video's source, deterministic. `media_id`: a pooled item, placed or not, whole; `layer_id`: a VideoClip, clipped to the source it plays, plus its `mapping` (t = t_start_us + (src - src_in_us) / rate). Returns `{ media_id, mapping?, shots: [{ index, src_start_us, src_end_us, src_keyframe_us, brightness, motion, sharpness, flags }], cut_scores: [{ src_us, score }], spans? }`, source µs; `score` 0..1. Stats from 3 frames/shot: `brightness` midpoint mean luma 0..1; `motion` 1 - SSIM of the end frames; `sharpness` Laplacian variance, relative per source. `flags`: "black" (all 3 < luma 0.02), "freeze" (SSIM >= 0.985), "fade" (monotonic luma ramp >= 0.15 touching < 0.10). Dark/blurry/frozen spots in shots: `passes: ["spans"]` samples every `step_us` into `spans: [{ kind, src_start_us, src_end_us, value }]`: "dark" luma < 0.08 >= 0.5 s (value: mean), "soft" sharpness < 35% of source median >= 1 s (value: ratio), "frozen" adjacent SSIM >= 0.985 >= 1 s (value: min). `passes` default shots, stats, events; `["shots"]` = timing only. To split: `auto_split_by_shot`.

layer_id.description:
A VideoClip: the answer is clipped to the source it plays and carries
its `mapping`.

media_id.description: A pooled video, scanned whole (placed or not).

min_shot_us.description:
Minimum shot duration (microseconds); cuts closer than this are merged.
Default 500000 (0.5 seconds).

passes.description:
Which passes to run. Default shots, stats, events; `["shots"]` is
timing only (no frame sampling). `"spans"` is opt-in: one sampled
decode of the source for dark / soft / frozen spans.

sensitivity.description:
Cut sensitivity in [0.0, 1.0]: a frame whose shot-change score exceeds
this starts a new shot. Lower = more (finer) cuts. Default 0.4.

step_us.description:
The spans pass's sampling step (microseconds), 100000..=10000000.
Default 500000. Needs `"spans"` in `passes`.

tools.name: compare_frames
tools.description: Compare two video frames for perceptual similarity — dedup shots, match a cutaway. Each side is `{ media_id | layer_id, src_us }`: a pooled video (placed or not) or a VideoClip, and a source µs time (the space of `analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` and `media://{id}/frame/{src_us}`); the two may be one source or two. Returns `{ phash_hamming, ssim, similar }`: `phash_hamming` is the 0..64 distance between the frames' perceptual hashes (0 = identical, 20+ = a different scene), `ssim` is structural similarity 0..1, and `similar` is `phash_hamming <= 10 && ssim >= 0.5`. Read-only; video only, errors naming the offending side.

layer_id.description: Or a VideoClip, read for its source.

src_us.description:
Source-absolute microseconds of the frame to sample (the space
`analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` uses).

layer_id.description: Or a VideoClip, read for its source.

src_us.description:
Source-absolute microseconds of the frame to sample (the space
`analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` uses).

tools.name: import_media
tools.description: Import media files: every path is checked first (a directory, missing or unreadable file refuses the call, nothing imported), then each is hashed, probed and copied into the project's Media/ folder. Returns `{ media: [record] }` in path order, each the pooled record with `derivatives`; `path` / `path_rel` name the Media/ copy (`copying: true` while it lands). A pooled file answers `existing: true` (a repeat is harmless), a missing one now read from here `relinked: true`; `same_content_as` names copies of its bytes. .srt/.vtt/.ass pool for `apply_subtitles`; .svg rasterises to PNG. Unrecorded.

paths.description: 1–50 video / audio / image / subtitle files the host can read: absolute, or relative to the open project's folder.

tools.name: extract_clip_audio
tools.description: Extract the ORIGINAL source audio that plays on a VideoClip or Audio layer (a VideoClip through its linked Audio member) — before gain, mute, effects or mixing — for an agent running its own speech model; no engine or API key is involved and nothing is uploaded. Returns a JSON metadata block (`layer_id`, `media_id`, `t_start_us`, `t_end_us`, `src_in_us`, `src_out_us`, `duration_us`, `rate` {num, den}, `sample_rate_hz`, `channels`, `bits_per_sample`, `byte_length`, `mime_type`) plus an MCP audio block: base64 WAV, mono 16 kHz 16-bit, starting at zero — about 2.6 MB of base64 per 60 s. Optional `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` are timeline µs, defaulting to the layer endpoints; at most 60 s of source audio per call (timeline windows ≤ 60 s / rate), so a long clip is several calls. Map a WAV offset `w` to the timeline as `t_start_us + w / rate`, then `apply_transcripts`. Refuses a layer that plays no sound and a window outside the layer.

layer_id.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

t_end_us.description:
Exclusive window end in the owning composition's absolute microseconds.
Defaults to the layer end. Maximum window duration: 60000000 us (60 s).

t_start_us.description:
Window start in the owning composition's absolute microseconds.
Defaults to the layer start. Must lie inside the layer.

tools.name: transcribe_clip
tools.description: Transcribe the audio that plays on 1–20 VideoClip or Audio layers (a VideoClip through its linked Audio member). Returns `{ transcripts: [{ source: { layer_id, signature }, backend, segments: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us, text, words: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us, text }] }], language, word_timing }], failed? }`, one per layer in order, timeline µs; hand `transcripts` to `apply_transcripts` as is. Cut pauses first, caption after: a clip changed since is refused there. `failed` lists layers that refused, with why. `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` narrow one layer's window. `language` is BCP-47; a model that does not cover it, or the language it detects, refuses with options. `whisper_cpp` and `funasr` run on this machine; `openai` (cloud) and `byo_endpoint` (the user's server) UPLOAD the audio — name one in `backend` only with the user's consent. Without `backend` the model selected in Settings runs, never another; if it cannot, the refusal names what it lacks and the ready engines. A retry after a client timeout joins the running job.

backend.description:
Strict engine override; that engine serves or the call errors.
`openai` and `byo_endpoint` upload the audio.

language.description: Spoken language, BCP-47 (`"en"`, `"zh-CN"`). Auto-detect when omitted.

layer_ids.description:
VideoClip or Audio layers to transcribe (1–20); one envelope each, in
this order. A VideoClip is read through its linked Audio member.

normalize_audio.description:
Explicit opt-in: normalize only the transcription copy toward -3 dBFS
peak, at most +24 dB. Original media/timeline stay unchanged. Default false.

t_end_us.description:
Optional window end (exclusive), timeline µs; one layer only. Defaults
to the layer's `t_end_us`. Must lie within the layer.

t_start_us.description:
Optional window start, timeline µs; one layer only. Defaults to the
layer's `t_start_us`. Must lie within the layer.

word_timestamps.description:
Ask for exact per-word times where the engine can emit them. Default
true; `false` forces SRT-style interpolated words. The result's
`word_timing` reports what you got.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Synthesize speech with the configured cloud TTS provider (OpenAI tts-1; the text is uploaded) and place it as a voiceover Audio layer, one placement or none: a refused placement leaves nothing in the pool. `text` ≤ 4096 chars; `voice`; optional `speed` 0.25..4.0 (default ≈ 1.0); `composition_id` (default root); `t_start_us` (default: the composition's duration, so it appends); `target_track_id`, else the topmost unlocked track whose audio lane is free across the clip, else a new 'Voiceover' track. The MP3 is cached by `(model, voice, speed, text)`, so a repeat costs no API request. Returns `{ layer_id, media_id, track_id, t_start_us, t_end_us, cached }`.

composition_id.description: A Group's composition to place in; omit for the root.

speed.description: 0.25..4.0 for tts-1. Omit to use the provider default (~1.0).

t_start_us.description:
Timeline start, µs. Defaults to the composition's `duration_us`, so
the voiceover appends at the end.

target_track_id.description:
Track to place on. Omitted: the topmost unlocked track whose audio lane
is free across the clip, else a new 'Voiceover' track.

text.description: Text to synthesize. tts-1 caps at 4096 characters.

tools.name: describe_clip
tools.description: Describe a video's visual content as timestamped segments with a video-understanding model (local Qwen3-VL / MiniCPM-V, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Name a pooled item by `media_id` (placed or not; the whole source by default) or a VideoClip by `layer_id` (the source it plays, plus its `mapping`, as `analyze_clip`'s). Samples the window at `fps` (default 1.0), ≤3600 frames per call. Returns `{ backend, model, summary?, media_id, mapping?, segments: [{ src_start_us, src_end_us, text, tags }] }`, source µs; `text` is prose, `tags` short visual keywords; long windows add a `summary`. Cached per source range, so a retry after a client timeout or an interruption resumes; `refresh` re-describes. `src_start_us`/`src_end_us` (e.g. a shot's) narrow the window; `focus` steers `tags`; `language` is BCP-47 (default: UI language). `qwen3_vl` and `minicpm_v` run on this machine; `byo_endpoint` UPLOADS frames — name it only with the user's consent. `backend` REQUIRES that engine, never substituting; omitted: the selected engine, then availability (local first).

backend.description:
Strict engine override; that engine serves or the call errors.
`byo_endpoint` uploads frames.

focus.description:
`shot-type` biases `tags` toward shot type / camera. Default: the app's
setting, else `general`. Cache key.

fps.description:
Frames sampled per second (higher = finer, more requests). Default:
the app's setting, else 1.0. Cache key.

language.description:
BCP-47 tag the `text` and `tags` come back in (`"en-US"`, `"zh-CN"`,
`"ja"`). Default: the app's UI language. Cache key.

layer_id.description:
Or a VideoClip: the default window is the source it plays, and the
answer carries its `mapping`.

media_id.description: A pooled video, described whole by default (placed or not).

refresh.description:
Describe again even when cached, replacing the earlier run (default
false).

src_end_us.description:
Optional exclusive window end, source-absolute microseconds. Defaults to
the end of the source the layer plays. Must lie within it.

src_start_us.description:
Optional window start, source-absolute microseconds (the space the
answer's segments and `analyze_clip`'s shots use). Defaults to the start
of the source the layer plays. Must lie within it.

resources.name: Composition
resources.description: Canvas size, fps, sample rate, color space, background.

resources.name: Media pool
resources.description: The media pool keyed by media id; each row is the item with its `media_id` and `derivatives` (waveform, conform, thumbnails, proxy: pending, running, ready or failed).

resources.name: Tracks
resources.description: Tracks with layer envelopes. Read project://layers/{id} for full layer detail.

resources.name: Compositions
resources.description: Every composition — the root and each Group — with composition_id, label, duration_us and ref_count (how many CompositionRef layers place it). project://tracks?composition=<id> and project://markers?composition=<id> read one of them; unscoped they read the root.

resources.name: History
resources.description: Recent operations and this opening's named checkpoints (no snapshots). `ops` is a window: `window_start` is the absolute stack index of `ops[0]`, and `cursor` is absolute too — never an offset into `ops`. `jump_to` takes an op's `op_id`, which no eviction shifts. `evicted` > 0 means the oldest entries were dropped for good.

resources.name: Audio mix plan
resources.description: Compiled export-audio mix plan (layer placement on the 48 kHz frame grid + envelope summaries) — for agents that want structural reasoning about what export will mix.

resources.name: Audio meter
resources.description: Latest preview master-bus level reading (rms/peak dBFS). `live: false` when nothing has played in the last 2 seconds.

prompts.name: cut-pauses
prompts.description: Cut the pauses out of a clip and close the gaps, tightening it. Or tack them first, so the user reviews every pause before any of it goes.

arguments.name: clip
arguments.description: The clip to tighten, as you would name it: its label, or what it shows or says. Omit for the clip you mean in the conversation.

arguments.name: threshold_db
arguments.description: Peak threshold, dBFS (≤ 0). Omit for the default.

arguments.name: min_pause_us
arguments.description: Shortest pause to cut, in microseconds. Omit for the default.

arguments.name: pad_us
arguments.description: Microseconds of each pause kept on each side when cutting. Omit for the default.

prompts.name: auto-caption
prompts.description: Transcribe a clip with the configured engine, then lay the transcript on the caption tracks with its word timing.

arguments.name: clip
arguments.description: The clip to caption, as you would name it: its label, or what it shows or says. Omit for the clip you mean in the conversation.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Optional language hint (en, zh, …). Auto-detect when omitted.

prompts.name: voiceover
prompts.description: Generate cloud TTS for a script and attach it as an Audio layer.

arguments.name: voice
arguments.description: OpenAI voice: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, or shimmer.

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: Optional speech speed in [0.25, 4.0]. Omit for the provider default.

arguments.name: track
arguments.description: Optional track to place it on, by its name. Omit for the default lane.
